\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Setup}
\label{sec:exp-setup}

We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across six models, three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 condition-evaluations (${\sim}$1,250 unique instances), with diagnostic analyses of confirmation bias and process-level independence (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).

\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq} (7B--32B). We additionally evaluate SCB universality via cross-model extraction on five frontier models (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1, gpt-5.5, o3, Gemini-2.5-Pro; Table~\ref{tab:frontier-scb}), where Mistral-7B extracts constraints from the target model's traces since closed-source APIs do not expose internals suitable for self-extraction.

\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n{=}204$, with gold logical annotations), ProofWriter depth-5~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n{=}600$), LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n{=}200$). StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n{=}200$) serves as a domain-formalizability diagnostic. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} ($n{=}30$) and AIME 2024 ($n{=}22$) probe the degenerate regime ($C_0 < 5\%$).

\paragraph{Parameters.} $K{=}12$ traces at $T{=}0.7$, extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}{=}0.3$, $\alpha{=}0.5$, Z3 timeout 10s. McNemar exact test ($\alpha{=}0.05$); 95\% bootstrap CIs ($10{,}000$ resamples) for $n \geq 200$. SICA incurs $4.5{\times}$ SC wall-clock; extraction accounts for 76\% of overhead.


\subsection{Main Results}
\label{sec:main-results}

\looseness=-1 No non-degenerate condition shows a significant SICA effect after FDR control (BH, $m{=}16$). Two show nominally significant degradation: Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($-2.83$\,pp, raw $p = 0.014$) and Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter ($-2.50$\,pp, raw $p = 0.011$); adjusted $p = 0.112$ for both. The intermediate-SC region (50--60\%) contains the only positive trends, none reaching $p < 0.05$. An aggregate sign test across self-extraction conditions yields 5 positive and 10 negative $\Delta$ values ($p = 0.30$, two-sided); including all conditions gives 8+/15$-$ ($p = 0.21$). Three-seed replication on Mistral-7B confirms seed-level noise: two of three seeds produce null or negative $\Delta$ (mean $+0.16 \pm 2.70$\,pp; Table~\ref{tab:multi-seed}). Four-seed replication on Qwen2.5-14B $\times$ FOLIO confirms the single-seed pattern: $\Delta \in [0.00, -2.01]$\,pp (mean $-1.24 \pm 0.86$; Table~\ref{tab:multi-seed}). TOST equivalence tests \citep{lakens2017equivalence} with margin $\pm 2$\,pp confirm 4 equivalent, 2 genuinely different (both negative), 10 underpowered. For the 10 underpowered conditions, our tests cannot rule out effects smaller than 1.86--4.84\,pp at 80\% power; the largest study ($n{=}804$) achieves MDE $= 1.86$\,pp (Appendix~\ref{app:power}). Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence for small effects. Margin sensitivity is robust: at $\pm 1$\,pp, 0/16 equivalent; at $\pm 3$\,pp, 10/16 equivalent; no margin yields a significant positive effect (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:tost-sensitivity}). We adopt $\pm 2$\,pp based on the lower bound of SC literature gains (2--5\,pp \citep{wang2023sc}), acknowledging this choice is anchored to SC effect sizes. We trace the failure below.


\subsection{Oracle Control}
\label{sec:oracle}

\looseness=-1 Replacing self-extracted constraints with gold annotations (FOLIO logical formulae, ProofWriter DSL), Oracle-SICA yields $+29.90$\,pp on Mistral-7B FOLIO ($p < 10^{-13}$), $+14.22$\,pp on Qwen2.5-14B FOLIO ($p = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}$), and $+17.17$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 10^{-14}$). Z3 agrees with gold labels on 95.1\% (FOLIO) and 97.1\% (ProofWriter). The MAX-SAT mechanism is sound; Mistral-7B's best self-extracted $\Delta$ ($+3.43$\,pp) captures only 11.5\% of its oracle ceiling. For Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter, the gap is wider still: self-extraction degrades accuracy ($-2.50$\,pp) against an oracle ceiling of $+17.17$\,pp, indicating that stronger models do not self-extract more effectively.

1	\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
2	
3	Test-time computation scaling through multiple reasoning samples has emerged as a practical alternative to scaling model parameters \citep{snell2025scaling, guo2025deepseekr1}.
4	The dominant aggregation strategy, Self-Consistency (SC) \citep{wang2023sc}, samples $K$ chain-of-thought traces and selects the majority answer.
5	SC is simple, model-agnostic, and effective---but it is hitting a ceiling.
6	\citet{loo2025reevaluating} demonstrate that gains from increasing $K$ plateau and even decline for strong models.
7	The gap between SC's theoretical promise (independent correct voters converge to truth) and its practical behavior (saturating gains) points to a structural mismatch: same-model traces carry correlated errors, and majority voting has no mechanism to correct shared bias.
8	
9	Confidence-weighted \citep{taubenfeld2025cisc} and universal \citep{chen2024usc} extensions alleviate this, but the core limitation persists.
10	Recent neuro-symbolic methods \citep{pan2023logiclm, olausson2023linc, xu2026dylos, li2025aristotle, wang2025fover, luo2025logicagent} report gains on logical reasoning but introduce components beyond the reasoning model.
11	A simpler question precedes these: can the \emph{same} model extract useful formal constraints from its own traces---a zero-cost upgrade requiring no additional model or data?
12	No prior work has systematically evaluated this.
13	
14	We ground our analysis in the Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) \citep{condorcet1785}: if $K$ independent voters each answer correctly with probability $p > 0.5$, the majority converges to truth \citep{austensmith1996}.
15	When independence fails \citep{ladha1992correlated}, additional samples carry diminishing information.
16	Measuring inter-trace agreement with Fleiss' $\kappa$ \citep{fleiss1971kappa}, we find $\kappa = 0.21$--$0.82$ across instruction-tuned conditions, yielding $K_{\text{eff}}$ as an ordinal diagnostic of vote diversity ($K_{\text{eff}} \approx 1.2$--$3.6$ for nominal $K = 12$; \S\ref{sec:condorcet}).
17	Chain-of-thought cosine similarity ($0.69$) far exceeds answer-level $\kappa$ ($0.46$), revealing that traces share reasoning processes even when they diverge on final answers (\S\ref{sec:process-kappa}).
18	When the same model extracts logical constraints from these correlated traces, the constraints exhibit \emph{symbolic confirmation bias} (SCB): on problems where the model errs, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratios $1.66$--$4.97\times$ across nine models), and 94\% of errors overlap with SC (\S\ref{sec:confirmation-bias}).
19	A shuffle control shows this bias is structural: it reflects the trace-count distribution rather than extraction-specific error.
20	Self-extraction cannot supply the independent signal that CJT requires.
21	
22	We study this through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts logical constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT (\S\ref{sec:pipeline}; Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
23	Across six open-source models (7B--32B), three domains (FOLIO \citep{han2022folio}, ProofWriter \citep{tafjord2021proofwriter}, LogiQA \citep{liu2020logiqa}), and over 3,000 condition-evaluations with four-seed replication, twenty-seven training-free remediation strategies spanning fifteen families all produce neutral or negative results (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}).
24	Prior work shows LLMs struggle with natural-language self-correction \citep{huang2024selfcorrect} and that LLM-generated logical formulas can be unreliable \citep{stechly2025selfverification}. Our formal channel is provably sound---the failure is precisely localizable to the extraction step. The assumption that formalizing reasoning provides \emph{independent} verification evidence fails not because Z3 is unreliable (99\% of constraints are syntactically valid), but because extraction inherits the model's biases: MAX-SAT produces answers identical to count-only aggregation on 94.4\% of problems, rendering the formal layer vacuous.
25	
26	Oracle controls confirm the mechanism is sound ($+29.90$\,pp Mistral-7B, $+14.22$\,pp Qwen-14B on FOLIO, $p < 0.001$; \S\ref{sec:oracle}), yet self-extraction captures only ${\sim}$12\% of this ceiling.
27	The central finding is a persistent independence-accuracy trade-off \citep{krogh1994neural}: Debate reduces $\kappa$ to 0.15 but collapses accuracy ($-18.6$\,pp); other methods cluster at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$, a same-model ceiling across three families (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).
28	A cross-architecture proof-of-concept escapes the bottleneck: DeBERTa NLI yields $+6.67$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), confirmed across three NLI architectures (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch}).
29	
30	Our contributions are:
31	\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
32	\item \textbf{Quantifying symbolic confirmation bias under formal verification.} While the general difficulty of LLM self-correction is known \citep{huang2024selfcorrect}, we provide the first quantitative characterization in the formal-verification setting: 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong answer (BR $1.66$--$4.97\times$ across nine models), yet 99\% pass Z3 validation. A shuffle control and MAX-SAT ablation show this bias is structural---the formal layer adds no information beyond majority voting. Twenty-seven training-free strategies fail to break it; cross-model extraction confirms universality across nine models from 7B to frontier (\S\ref{sec:confirmation-bias}).
33	
34	\item \textbf{Diagnostic toolkit for independence-accuracy trade-offs.} We adapt the known diversity--accuracy trade-off \citep{krogh1994neural} to LLM self-extraction, contributing three practical diagnostics ($K_\text{eff}$, BR, $C_0$) that predict when symbolic aggregation will fail. 36	\item \textbf{Process-level independence analysis.} CoT cosine similarity ($0.69$--$0.79$) exceeds answer-level $\kappa$ ($0.45$--$0.74$) across four models from three families; under cross-model extraction on frontier models, SICA gain decreases monotonically with process similarity ($\rho = -1.0$, $p = 0.008$; \S\ref{sec:process-kappa}).

Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting over chain-of-thought traces saturates as sample count grows because same-model traces are correlated voters.
We investigate whether symbolic constraint extraction can break this plateau through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts logical constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT.
Across six open-source LLMs (7B--32B) on three logical reasoning domains with over 3,000 condition-evaluations (${\sim}$1,250 unique instances), we find no evidence of improvement (aggregate sign test: 5+/10$-$, $p = 0.30$; none of sixteen non-degenerate conditions shows a significant positive effect after FDR control), with equivalence established in four conditions, significant degradation in two, and ten remaining underpowered for effects below ${\sim}$5\,pp.
We trace the failure to \emph{symbolic confirmation bias} (SCB): on incorrect problems, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratios ranging from $1.66\times$ to $4.97\times$), but a shuffle control shows this bias is structural---it reflects trace-count distributions rather than extraction-specific error ($\text{BR}_\text{obs} \approx \text{BR}_\text{null}$, $p > 0.7$). MAX-SAT produces answers identical to count-only aggregation on 94.4\% of problems, confirming that the formal verification layer adds no information beyond majority voting despite 99\% of constraints passing Z3 validation.
Cross-model extraction confirms SCB universality across nine models from 7B to frontier (BR $1.66$--$4.97\times$), though frontier models use cross-model rather than self-extraction.
Twenty-seven training-free remediation strategies spanning fifteen families all fail, confirming a persistent independence-accuracy trade-off.
Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound ($+29.90$\,pp, $+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+17.17$\,pp ProofWriter; $p < 0.001$); same-model self-extraction captures only ${\sim}$12\% of this ceiling.
Cross-architecture NLI verification on propositional-logic benchmarks escapes the bottleneck when the verifier exceeds the generator ($+6.67$\,pp, $p < 0.001$), with gain monotonically ordered by the capability gap ($p = 0.003$, $n{=}6$).

\looseness=-1 All 27 training-free remediation strategies spanning four categories produce neutral-to-negative results (Figure~\ref{fig:interventions-summary}; Appendices~\ref{app:extraction}--\ref{app:entropy}). We highlight four representative failure modes that illuminate the independence-accuracy trade-off:

\looseness=-1 \emph{Debate} ($\kappa = 0.15$, $\Delta = -18.6$\,pp): successfully breaks trace correlation by forcing adversarial positions, but accuracy collapses---the model cannot maintain coherent reasoning under forced disagreement. This reveals a fundamental tension: same-model diversity and quality are at odds.

\looseness=-1 \emph{Cross-model extraction} (using a different LLM to extract constraints from the generator's traces): $\kappa$ decreases slightly but $\Delta \approx 0$, because models from the same training family share systematic biases that persist across architectures (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}).

\looseness=-1 \emph{Contrastive prompting} (eliciting pro/con constraints): produces imbalanced output (94 pro vs.\ 65 con constraints on Mistral-7B FOLIO), indicating that confirmation bias transfers from answer generation to constraint generation.

\looseness=-1 \emph{Oracle ceiling}: gold-annotated constraints yield $+29.90$\,pp (Mistral-7B FOLIO), proving the MAX-SAT mechanism is sound. Self-extraction captures only ${\sim}$12\% of this ceiling, precisely localizing the bottleneck to extraction quality rather than aggregation.

\looseness=-1 All non-debate strategies cluster at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$, a same-model ceiling across three families (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}). No individual strategy achieves significance after correction (Appendix~\ref{app:intervention-individual}). Trained extractors remain the most promising direction for closing the oracle gap.

lines: We distinguish three paradigms. \emph{Specification-generation} (Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}, LINC \citep{olausson2023linc}, SatLM \citep{ye2024satlm}) translates problem descriptions into formal specifications before any answer is generated; LINC documents ${\sim}$40\% translation errors even at this level. \emph{Program-generation} \citep{gao2023pal,chen2023program,lyu2023faithful} produces executable code from problem statements. Both paradigms access the problem before generating candidate answers. \emph{Trace-extraction} (this work) operates post-hoc on reasoning traces that already contain candidates, inheriting confirmation bias (\S\ref{sec:confirmation-bias}). SatLM provides a natural control: it succeeds because problem-level formalization precedes answer generation, whereas trace-level extraction cannot avoid contamination (\S\ref{sec:mirage}). Recent extensions \citep{ryu2025clover, xu2026dylos, li2025aristotle, wang2025fover, singh2026verge, luo2025logicagent, miya2025eidoku} introduce capabilities beyond the reasoning model. \citet{amonkar2025realitycheck} show formalization degrades with complexity; \citet{chan2026position} argue logical soundness is unreliable for neurosymbolic verification. Our oracle controls confirm the mechanism is sound ($+29.90$/$+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+17.17$\,pp ProofWriter); the failure localizes to self-extraction (\S\ref{sec:oracle}).

-Scaling test-time computation through additional traces \citep{snell2025scaling} or structured search \citep{yao2023tree} faces the same correlation challenge: same-model attempts collapse into correlated solutions. Reasoning models (o1, DeepSeek-R1 \citep{guo2025deepseekr1}, QwQ \citep{qwen2024qwq}) extend thinking time but remain subject to correlated same-model voting: QwQ-32B produces $\kappa = 0.91$ and $C_0 = 2.6\%$, suggesting that longer reasoning chains intensify homogenization rather than alleviating it. Trained verifiers offer an alternative \citep{cobbe2021gsm8k, lightman2024prm, wang2024mathshepherd}; multi-agent debate refines answers through discussion \citep{liang2023encouraging, du2023improving}. Self-verification \citep{weng2023selfverification}, chain-of-verification \citep{dhuliawala2023chainofverification}, self-refinement \citep{madaan2023selfrefine}, tool-augmented critique \citep{gou2024critic}, and formal CoT verification \citep{zhu2025vericot} report gains, but none systematically tests self-extracted constraints under formal solvers. We find the bottleneck shifts from the verifier to the extractor: self-extracted constraints inherit the model's bias regardless of verification formalism (\S\ref{sec:confirmation-bias}). Self-correction without external feedback degrades performance \citep{huang2024selfcorrect, stechly2025selfverification}; \citet{valmeekam2023llms} further show fundamental planning limitations that compound self-verification failures. Our diagnostics (BR, Eff-$K$, process-$\kappa$) predict when trace-aggregation will fail.

CJT \citep{condorcet1785} guarantees convergence under independent voting; \citet{ladha1992correlated} show correlated voters reduce effective ensemble size. Classical ensemble diversity theory \citep{kuncheva2003measures, brown2005diversity} formalizes this intuition: diversity measures (e.g., $\kappa$-statistic, disagreement) predict ensemble gain. \section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

\subsection{Setup}
\label{sec:exp-setup}

We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across six models, three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 condition-evaluations (${\sim}$1,250 unique instances), with diagnostic analyses of confirmation bias and process-level independence (\S\ref{sec:analysis}).

\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq} (7B--32B). We additionally evaluate SCB universality via cross-model extraction on five frontier models (gpt-4o, gpt-4.1, gpt-5.5, o3, Gemini-2.5-Pro; Table~\ref{tab:frontier-scb}), where Mistral-7B extracts constraints from the target model's traces since closed-source APIs do not expose internals suitable for self-extraction.

\paragraph{Datasets.} FOLIO~\citep{han2022folio} ($n{=}204$, with gold logical annotations), ProofWriter depth-5~\citep{tafjord2021proofwriter} ($n{=}600$), LogiQA~\citep{liu2020logiqa} ($n{=}200$). StrategyQA~\citep{geva2021strategyqa} ($n{=}200$) serves as a domain-formalizability diagnostic. GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} ($n{=}30$) and AIME 2024 ($n{=}22$) probe the degenerate regime ($C_0 < 5\%$).

\paragraph{Parameters.} $K{=}12$ traces at $T{=}0.7$, extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}{=}0.3$, $\alpha{=}0.5$, Z3 timeout 10s. McNemar exact test ($\alpha{=}0.05$); 95\% bootstrap CIs ($10{,}000$ resamples) for $n \geq 200$. SICA incurs $4.5{\times}$ SC wall-clock; extraction accounts for 76\% of overhead.

\subsection{Oracle Control}
\label{sec:oracle}

\looseness=-1 Replacing self-extracted constraints with gold annotations (FOLIO logical formulae, ProofWriter DSL), Oracle-SICA yields $+29.90$\,pp on Mistral-7B FOLIO ($p < 10^{-13}$), $+14.22$\,pp on Qwen2.5-14B FOLIO ($p = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}$), and $+17.17$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 10^{-14}$). The MAX-SAT mechanism is sound; Mistral-7B's best self-extracted $\Delta$ ($+3.43$\,pp) captures only 11.5\% of its oracle ceiling. For Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter, the gap is wider still: self-extraction degrades accuracy ($-2.50$\,pp) against an oracle ceiling of $+17.17$\,pp, indicating that stronger models do not self-extract more effectively.
